findings.body:
**ItemRef keeps a list index, so a handle can point at a different item after a structural edit.**

`ItemRef` stores only a numeric index into `items`. Its `#path` getter (`src/queue-runner/queueCell.ts:245`) returns `['items', this.#index]` on every access. When an earlier item is removed with `cell.delete(['items'], 0)`, the item previously at index 1 moves to index 0, and a handle created with `cell.item(1)` now resolves to the item that was at index 2. A later `ref.set('state', ...)` then edits the wrong item.

The module header (lines 5–12) states that a handle taken before an edit "observes the edit after it, as a Python `item` reference does." A Python reference to a dict object keeps pointing at that object after a list deletion. The TypeScript handle does not, so the stated equivalence holds only for edits that leave the list order unchanged.

If the contract is meant to cover structural changes, the handle needs item identity or an explicit invalidation path. If callers never retain handles across deletion, insertion, reordering, or `adopt()`, the header should state that limit.

Callers were not established. The reviewed repository search for `.item(` and `ItemRef` returned only the definitions at `queueCell.ts:10`, `:195`, and `:235`. The search did not run in the sandbox for files outside `src/`, so out-of-tree callers remain unknown.
findings.title: ItemRef keeps a list index, so a handle can point at a different item after a structural edit.

findings.body:
**Serialize `QueueCell.launch` against edits made while it is pending.**

`launch` reads `this.#queue` at `src/queue-runner/queueCell.ts:220`, then awaits `reserveAndSpawnReview`. The public edit methods (`set`, `update`, `delete`, `pop`, `setdefault`, `append`, and `ItemRef.set`) run synchronously and reassign `this.#queue` through `#edit`. Nothing in the class blocks them during that await. An edit made in that window is overwritten at line 221 by a queue derived from the pre-edit snapshot. The catch path at line 224 can also replace newer edits with `lastSaved`.

No caller in `src/` invokes `QueueCell.launch` in the inspected source. The other `.launch(` matches are `effects.launch` and `fx.launch` in `src/queue-runner/startOne.ts:290` and `src/queue-runner/coverageUsage.ts:247`, which are different objects. The loss therefore depends on future callers that edit the cell during a launch. The class exposes this path, so the defect is latent but reachable through its public API.

Choose one contract and enforce it in code. Either reject edits and `adopt` calls while a launch is pending, or rebase the launch result onto the current queue instead of replacing it. The inspected code does not establish which contract the maintainers intend, so no diff is proposed.
findings.title: Serialize `QueueCell.launch` against edits made while it is pending.
Replace the `effects` spread with explicit delegation.

findings.body:
**Make a failed author diff throw instead of returning `nothing-to-review`.**

`diffHasPaths` is documented to return `false` when Git fails (`src/queue-runner/mergedAuthorPlan.ts:66-67`). `planAuthor` treats every `false` as an empty binding. It returns `nothing-to-review` with the reason `author binding has an empty diff` (lines 146-147). A failed diff therefore produces the same outcome as an empty range, and the reason text is wrong for the failure case. Callers cannot tell a Git error from a real empty range.

Return `false` only for a successful empty diff. Throw on Git failure. `planAuthor` does not catch the error, so it propagates to the caller.

<details>
<summary>Suggested contract change</summary>

```diff
-  /** `git diff --name-only base head` is non-empty; false when git fails (check=False). */
+  /** `git diff --name-only base head` is non-empty; throws when git fails, false only for an empty diff. */
   diffHasPaths(base: string, head: string): Promise<boolean>;
```

</details>
findings.title: Make a failed author diff throw instead of returning `nothing-to-review`.
